title: Forgiveness of Sin
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Forgiveness of sin means that God pardons the guilt of sinners through Jesus Christ and no longer holds their sins against them. Forgiveness is grounded in Christ’s blood, not in denial, excuses, or human worthiness.
summary: Forgiveness of sin means that God pardons the guilt of sinners through Jesus Christ and no longer holds their sins against them. Forgiveness is grounded in Christ’s blood, not in denial, excuses, or human worthiness.
christFocus: Jesus Christ secures forgiveness by bearing sin and shedding His blood for sinners. In Him, guilt is not hidden or minimized; it is removed by the mercy and justice of God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sin creates real guilt before God. Forgiveness is therefore not a small emotional relief but a divine pardon. God Himself removes guilt through the work of Christ.

Forgiveness is costly. Scripture connects forgiveness with redemption through Christ’s blood. God does not forgive by pretending sin is harmless, but by dealing with sin at the cross.

Forgiveness is full for those in Christ. God removes transgressions from His people as far as the east is from the west. The believer does not need to keep paying for sins Christ has borne.

Forgiveness also forms forgiving people. Those who have been pardoned by God are called to extend mercy to others, releasing vengeance to the Lord and refusing bitterness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people carry guilt as though their sin is too large for Christ. Others treat forgiveness lightly because they do not see what sin cost. This doctrine speaks to both: forgiveness is costly, and forgiveness is real.

For the ashamed, forgiveness means sin is not the final word. For the proud, forgiveness means no one stands before God without mercy. For the wounded, forgiveness opens the way to freedom from bitterness without denying justice.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Confess sin honestly and receive God’s forgiveness in Christ. Do not cover guilt with excuses or punish yourself as though Christ’s blood were not enough. As one forgiven by God, seek grace to forgive others wisely and truthfully, entrusting justice to the Lord.
